contract.reader: An engineering student or engineer with basic circuit analysis, calculus and elementary statistics who has to specify, read a datasheet for, or report a result from a sensor
contract.problem: Lacking a precise vocabulary for what a measurement is and how good a sensor is, and not knowing how to state an uncertainty
contract.outcome: Describe the measurement chain; distinguish sensor, transducer, actuator and self-generating vs modulating sensors; use the static characteristics and the first-order dynamic model; separate systematic from random error; build a GUM uncertainty budget and report U with k; do a two-point calibration; choose a sensor by a question list
contract.contribution: One running PT100 example carried through transfer function, sensitivity, nonlinearity, uncertainty and loading with every number computed; a worked budget showing where effort pays; unambiguous self-generating/modulating terms
contract.evidence: Worked calculations; IEC 60751:2022; JCGM 100:2008 (GUM); JCGM 200:2012 (VIM); Bentley (2005); Fraden (2016); Regtien and Dertien (2018)
contract.limitations: One sensor type worked in detail; second-order dynamics only described; no correlated contributions or degrees of freedom (series last entry); later chain stages deferred

findings.location: Section 3.1 R(100), Section 5.2 u_c and U, Section 6 two-point calibration (360 px; mobile-light-11, 21, 23)
findings.problem: The displays are cut at the right edge behind an unmarked scroll: = 138.51 ohm, U = k u_c, and = 1.0132 are hidden
findings.whyItMatters: Small: each value is restated nearby, but U = k u_c is the definition the section is about
findings.action: Put each pair on its own line, or a site-level scroll cue for wide equations
findings.acceptance: On new 360 px captures all three displays are fully visible, or a visible cue shows that they scroll

findings.location: Section 5.3 uncertainty budget table (360 px; mobile-light-21, 22)
findings.problem: Only Contribution, Information and Evaluation are visible; the Standard uncertainty column is beyond the scroll shadow
findings.whyItMatters: The column is the outcome of each row; values reappear in the next sentence, so the reader is slowed rather than misled
findings.action: Merge Evaluation and Standard uncertainty into one column so three columns fit at 360 px
findings.acceptance: At 360 px every standard uncertainty in the table is visible without scrolling

findings.location: Section 3.3 PT100 nonlinearity plot (360 px; mobile-light-13)
findings.problem: The generated figure keeps its 26rem minimum width; the axis stops at 80 degC, the axis label reads tem, and the return to zero at 100 degC is hidden
findings.whyItMatters: The caption says the error is zero at both ends; the phone reader sees only one
findings.action: Site-level scroll cue or lower minimum width for generated figures
findings.acceptance: At 360 px the whole plot is visible, or a visible cue shows that it scrolls

findings.location: Section 3.1 first sentence; Section 4 link to Foundations of Control Systems
findings.problem: Transfer function here means the static characteristic curve, while the linked control series defines it as the Laplace-domain G(s); the page does not say the uses differ
findings.whyItMatters: A reader following the link meets the same bold term with a different definition, in the section where both meanings apply
findings.action: Add a clause in 3.1 marking this as the static sense, distinct from the dynamic transfer function of the control series, or say static transfer function at first use
findings.acceptance: The live page's Section 3.1 distinguishes the static sense of the term from the dynamic transfer function
